commands.cross_library: python benchmarks/compare.py --libraries numpy unitx pint astropy unyt --sizes scalar 1 1000 1000000 --repeat 7 --label current

notes: Current source only. Two built-in-backend runs, one cross-library run with SymPy, and one array-write run.
Source snapshots selected through PYTHONPATH. Installed unitx metadata in individual measurements does not identify measured source; source hashes do.
Shared-operation physical results validated before timing; imports/setup excluded. No concurrent tests or profiler during timing.
Tracemalloc peaks measured separately from timing. Single-machine observations without CPU/process controls or confidence intervals.
mean uses np.mean(q); mean_method calls q.mean() with the same prepared data and unit.

unit_algebra_experiment.candidate: working source with empty Monomial power reuse and identity-term filtering in Factor/Dimension
notes: Baseline source exported from the stated commit; candidate identified by content fingerprints. Use the same benchmark scripts and interpreter for both.
No tests or profilers ran concurrently with timing. Imports and input preparation are excluded. Tracemalloc measurements are separate from timing.
Summary tables use the median of two run medians. Each run records seven timing samples. There are no confidence intervals or timing thresholds.
The formula variants differ only in whether si.m**2 and si.cm**2 are built inside each call. Both evaluate a 1.5 m length squared plus 10000 cm2 to 3.25 m2.
Installed unitx distribution metadata in compare.py does not identify the source selected through PYTHONPATH. Use source_sha256.
Monomial exponent-one specialization was evaluated but omitted: Factor and Dimension already handle it; explicit Unit**1 and parser exponent-one inputs are the remaining internal callers.
Imports, input creation and one warm call precede each capture.
Workloads run sequentially without tests or other benchmarks.
Frame times are sampled wall time including profiler/harness overhead.
cProfile is a separate diagnostic pass; do not use either profiler for speedup claims.
Functions include descendant time: ancestor/descendant percentages overlap and must not be added.
Leaf-owner categories are disjoint call-site attribution. Native ufunc execution can be charged to the NumPy adapter frame; it is not all Python dispatch overhead.
Pyinstrument and cProfile both perturb call-heavy Python workloads. Their agreement identifies call chains, not uninstrumented runtime fractions or guaranteed speedups.
The numeric controls use the same exp(-x/2).mean pipeline with bare NumPy and wrapped inputs, alternating numpy/unitx/unitx/numpy with seven samples per run.

routing_experiment.baseline: Existing uncommitted working-tree snapshot at the start of this investigation; already contains the previous identity-product changes.
notes: Scalar/array runs alternate baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline; summaries are medians of the two run medians. Timing excludes imports, validation, tracing and profiling.
Editable installation metadata reports 0.14.0 in the original interpreter; source files and hashes, not that stale distribution metadata, identify the compared 0.17.9 working trees.
Each metadata variant uses the same candidate source except its three recorded files. Variant order is loop/comprehension/generator/stream, then reversed; each run has seven samples of 5000 calls.

generator materializes its filtered iterables with list() inside _product; stream uses iter()/next() to retain empty/single-term fast paths without a list. Temporary variants are experiments, not public alternatives.
The scalar formula still calls is_numpy_object ten times. Exact Python scalar types return before the MRO loop; no type cache or NumPy import is added.
Call counts use one separately warmed cProfile call; fit counts compare baseline finite differences with candidate analytic Jacobian, so they include both library and algorithm changes.

Fit timings compare finite differences and analytic derivatives on the same candidate source. Both include model, normalized residuals, solve and local covariance; the two modes agree on fitted parameters and covariance.
No timing thresholds or large-array numerical-kernel speedup are claimed.

checks: full pytest in all three environments, including source doctests and Pyright consumers
full Markdown doctest command in all three environments
ruff check, test annotation check, format check
limits: Python versions other than 3.12 were not tested in this investigation.
No SymPy environment was tested; all measurements and test suites use the built-in factorization backend.
No wheel/sdist release or publishing validation; this change adds no public library types or packaging changes.

operand_experiment.baseline: Uncommitted tree matching the routing_experiment candidate; HEAD 9e0fc3f
operand_experiment.candidate: Shared NumPy operand boundary and reuse of the first contraction unit
notes: Same Python 3.12.15 interpreter; baseline and candidate selected by PYTHONPATH from separate source exports.
Inputs, imports and correctness validation precede timing. Profiles and allocation tracing are separate from timing; tests and builds were stopped.
Summary values are medians of two run medians. CPU frequency and other machine processes remain uncontrolled.
The experiment combines operand-module extraction and contraction preparation. It does not isolate an elapsed-time benefit from file movement.
Large-array controls show run drift and do not establish a numerical-kernel speedup. Fits are effectively unchanged.
Source tests cover current/minimum dependencies and no NumPy; validation details are in performance.md.
